newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger says IMF, World Bank aid indispensable.
newsitem.headline: Niger says IMF, World Bank aid indispensable.

text.p: Niger President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara said on Thursday there was no alternative to austerity measures needed for IMF and World Bank aid.
"This aid is an indispensable incentive for mobilising support from other international donors whose only criteria are performance and competition," Mainassara told parliament.

In an address marking his first anniversary as elected president, the former military ruler called for greater belt-tightening given Niger's internal and external debts totalling 700 billion CFA francs ($1.1 billion).
He said a June 1996 Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility accord with the International Monetary Fund for a one-year period from March 1996 had already yielded benefits.
The West African country had received 56 billion CFA in budgetary assistance from foreign donors and debt relief of 67 billion CFA from the Paris Club of official creditors.
In addition, Niger was awaiting the disbursement of 90 billion CFA in aid from donors following the IMF's approval of the second Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, he said.

The president said Niger had embarked on about 15 development projects since major donors resumed aid disbursements, frozen after the former army chief seized power from an elected government in January 1996.
Mainassara was declared winner of presidential elections in July 1996, held after he locked up his civilian rivals. The United States denounced the poll and cut aid.

About 1,000 opposition supporters still protesting the outcome of that poll staged an anti-Mainassara march during the speech in which he promised regional and local elections in the first quarter of 1998.
